prompt: Implement an elevator state machine: given the current State enum value and a text command, return the next state, leaving the state unchanged for commands that do not apply. Complete next in Elevator.
explanation: A state machine pairs a current state with an input to pick the next state; here switch selects on the command string (Java switch supports String) while each case checks whether the transition applies to the current state. Enum values are singletons, so comparing them with == is safe and idiomatic. The default case handles every unknown command by returning current unchanged -- an explicit 'no transition' rule rather than an error.
hints: Java's switch works on Strings: switch (command) { case "up": ... default: ... }
Each case still has to look at the current state: "up" only moves the elevator when current == State.IDLE.
Enum comparison uses == (State.MOVING_UP etc.), and default: return current covers unknown commands.
